author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Adobe reported third-quarter revenue above Wall Street estimates Thursday and said annual recurring revenue from products built around generative AI more than doubled from a year earlier.

Revenue totaled $6.76 billion, compared with an average analyst estimate of $6.70 billion compiled by LSEG. Adjusted profit was $6.13 per share, also ahead of the $6.09 estimate. The results indicate that AI features are beginning to contribute more meaningfully to Adobe’s subscription business.

For the fourth quarter, the company forecast revenue of $6.80 billion to $6.85 billion. The midpoint, $6.825 billion, was slightly below the $6.85 billion analyst estimate. Reuters reported that Adobe shares fell 1.9% in extended trading; that move was a reported after-hours figure, not a live quote.

Adobe also said Anil Chakravarthy will become chief executive on December 1, while longtime leader Shantanu Narayen will move to executive chair. The transition arrives as the company tries to turn AI tools into durable growth while facing competition from a new generation of design and content-creation services.
dek: Quarterly sales and adjusted profit topped expectations, while the midpoint of Adobe’s next-quarter revenue forecast came in slightly below analysts’ estimate.
headline: Adobe revenue beats estimates as AI-first recurring sales double
